messages:
maria: Hey folks — hit a reproducible weirdness with redwoodctl + localtest on mac. Installed via brew, then when I run `redwoodctl localserve` and later use `sudo` for unrelated stuff my shell gets re-sourced and redwoodctl loses the active profile, causing it to prompt for login again. super noisy during dev loops :/

maria: Repro steps: brew install redwoodctl -> open new terminal (zsh) -> run `redwoodctl localserve --profile dev` -> in another tab run `sudo launchctl kickstart -k system/org.some.service` (any sudo) -> back in localserve tab you see a login prompt from redwoodctl.

maria: Output snippet:
```
$ redwoodctl localserve --profile dev
Starting local server (profile=dev)
Serving on http://localhost:7788
[auth] profile lost: no credentials found, please run `redwoodctl login`
```

maria: I traced it to our install writing a shim into /etc/zshrc.d/ and also dropping a small `/etc/profile.d/redwoodctl.sh` that sets REDWOOD_PROFILE by default. When sudo runs some shells re-eval system rc which ends up clobbering the user-level env var (or creating a new empty one), so the runtime interprets it as ‘no profile’.

maria: current system file:
```
# /etc/profile.d/50_redwoodctl.sh
export REDWOOD_PROFILE=default
```

maria: This seems brittle for multi-user machines or when developers rely on explicit per-shell profiles. Anyone seen this pattern before?

tanner: ugh yeah saw something similar with another tool — system-level env files are dangerous. two quick questions: 1) can you reproduce without brew (tarball)? 2) what shell and sudo config are you on? eg sudoers env_keep, or are you on mac where sudo resets env?

maria: 1) reproduced with upstream tarball (same behaviour). 2) macos 12.6, zsh, default sudo (no env_keep configured). Also happens with `sudo -s` vs `sudo <cmd>` — any sudo that touches the session triggers it.

devex-bot: Thanks for the report — tagging @devex for triage and adding label: install-config

oscar: thanks for the writeup, maria. two quick mitigation options until we fix installer: 1) remove the /etc/profile.d file and put a user-level helper at ~/.config/redwood/profile or 2) change the installer to write the default into /usr/local/etc/redwoodctl/default_profile and have redwoodctl prefer an explicit env var only if set by the user. both avoid stomping during sudo.

oscar: short-term workaround: edit /etc/profile.d/50_redwoodctl.sh -> `unset REDWOOD_PROFILE` or replace with a default only if not already set: `: ${REDWOOD_PROFILE:=default}` (though that still influences sessions started by sudo on mac).

maria: good suggestions. I tried `: ${REDWOOD_PROFILE:=default}` and it helped a bit but some sudo path still gets an empty var. removing the file entirely fixes it for my flow.

tanner: we should also consider changing redwoodctl login to fall back to checking ~/.config/redwood/active_profile before failing, rather than treating the env var as the single source of truth. that would make it robust against env resets.

oscar: agree. created an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cli/issues/1427 (installer: avoid system-level REDWOOD_PROFILE env leak). will draft a small PR for installer and a separate runtime change to prefer explicit config file.

ci-bot: CI run queued for branch installer-profile-fix (#1428) — builds will run on darwin/linux.

maria: awesome — thanks! one more ask: could we document this in the quickstart troubleshooting section? spent a bit figuring out it was the system rc. a tiny note about `sudo` re-sourcing behavior and the profile precedence would save future folks time.

oscar: yup, will add a short note in docs + a fix in the installer PR. thanks for the detailed repro, that made triage quick. :thumbsup:
